title: Latency SLA breach events are not attributable to any pipe/node (pipe:-1, node:-1)
evidence:
scripts/sim/sim_core.gd:412-415:
	if latency > _latency_tol_ticks(pkt.cls) and not bool(s.lat_breach):
		s.lat_breach = true
		s.lat_tick = tick
		s.events.append({"tick": tick, "kind": "latency", "pipe": -1, "node": -1})

contrast, loss events (sim_core.gd:477) do carry attribution:
			s.events.append({"tick": tick, "kind": "loss", "pipe": pipe_id, "node": node})
detail: Epic test contract: 'SLA breach is detectable and attributable'. Loss breaches record pipe+node; latency breach events hardcode pipe/node -1 and the breaching packet is erased on delivery, so latency breaches cannot be attributed anywhere.
recommended_fix: Record the delivering packet's last pipe (pkt.pipe) and far endpoint node in the latency event instead of -1, matching the loss-event attribution shape.

evidence:
scripts/capture_runner.gd:98-102:

	_rig.frame_point(_arc_mid(spine[0], spine[1]), 1)

capture_runner.gd:108-110 (set_lanes only AFTER the shot):
	await _settle(6)
	main._on_qos_apply(pipe_id, [50, 30, 20], {"email": 2, "streaming": 0})
	await _settle(6)

sim_balance.gd:54,65 — speed is per LANE, defaults put both classes on one lane:
const LANE_SPEED_MILLI := [200, 100, 60] # travel milli-units per tick, by lane (speed = priority)
const DEFAULT_ALLOC := [0, 100, 0]
detail: Briefing A2: 'packets visibly stream along arcs at class-dependent speed'. Shot 06 is captured pre-set_lanes; with DEFAULT_ALLOC both classes ride Standard (LANE_SPEED_MILLI[1]), so all dots move at one speed — the comment's claim doesn't hold.
recommended_fix: Take the packet-flow capture after applying a multi-lane allocation (classes on different lanes), or relabel shot 06 as uniform Standard-speed streaming.

title: classify() comments claim pipe-select is pinnable there, but classify() never returns SELECT
evidence:
scripts/input_router.gd:7-9 (header):
## orbit); press anywhere else = ORBIT. One positional rule, no modes. The
## decision is factored into the static classify() so the headless suite can
## pin the contract.

input_router.gd:34-38 — classify() has no SELECT branch:
## THE rule: a node hit draws, a pipe hit selects, anything else orbits.
static func classify(collider: Object) -> Mode:
	if collider is NodeSite:
		return Mode.DRAW
	return Mode.ORBIT
detail: E2.3 'QoS panel on pipe select' is implemented, but the stated headless-pinnable contract doesn't cover it: the SELECT decision actually lives in _begin() via flow_view.pick_pipe, not in static classify(). Comment contradicts the code.
recommended_fix: Fix the comments to state pipe-hit SELECT is decided in _begin() by geometric pick_pipe (pipes have no physics collider), or move the decision into classify().
